title: Verified platform installation plan v1
description: The typed sequence of operations one release performs on one platform profile, and what each one reverses to. docs/architecture/PLATFORM_KEY_AND_PRIVILEGE_MATRIX.md and ADR-010 through ADR-013 are the normative owners; packages/schemas/planning-schema.sql#platform_install_plans and #platform_install_operations are the persistence owners. Every operation is a named platform mechanism rather than a generic lifecycle verb or a script, because "install the service" is what lets three platforms claim one behaviour they do not share, and because a script is not something a validator can check the reversal of. The plan is verified before it runs: the release signature is checked first, always, and the operation that does so is the only one permitted at sequence 1.

requires_privileged_consent.description: True only for a plan containing register-privileged-supervisor. D-067 makes machine-wide supervision separately consented and least-privilege, so a plan that quietly needed it would be the consent failure rather than an installation detail.

sequence.description: Dense from 1 within a plan. Sequence 1 is verify-release-signature and nothing else, so no plan can place a filesystem write before the check that decides whether the release is genuine.

irreversible.description: True when the operation has no reversal — either because it changes nothing, as a verification does, or because its effect cannot be undone. Every other operation names the reversal a rollback runs. A rollback that discovers the answer at run time is D-074's failure mode rather than its contract: automatic binary rollback is permitted only while the previous release stays read/write compatible, and an operation with no reversal is what ends that permission.

mechanism.description: The exact operating-system mechanism, named rather than implied: launchd-user, systemd-user, systemd-system, windows-service, windows-scheduled-task. D-013 forbids claiming equal strength across platforms, and a plan that did not name the mechanism would be doing exactly that.
